problem: Find the horizontal asymptote of $y=f(x)$ where $f(x)=\frac{7{x}^{5}-3{x}^{2}}{6-2x}.$
worked_solution:
The horizontal asymptote is $y={lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x).$ To find the horizontal asymptote, we apply the usual procedure of dividing the numerator and denominator by the highest power of $x$ in the denominator, which is $x.$

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \infty }f(x) & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{7{x}^{5}-3{x}^{2}}{6-2x} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(\frac{7{x}^{5}}{x}-\frac{3{x}^{2}}{x})}{(\frac{6}{x}-\frac{2x}{x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(7{x}^{4}-3x)}{(\frac{6}{x}-2)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to \infty }\frac{(7{x}^{4}-3x)}{0-2} \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}{lim}_{x\to \infty }(7{x}^{4}-3x) \\  & =-\infty .\end{aligned}
$$

 

The limit does not come out to a finite number. Therefore, there is no horizontal asymptote.
